d: Use state machines in the Animation Graph Editor to organize state-driven animations and control how they transition.
h:
A state machine combines animation nodes into named states, such as Idle, Walk, Run, and Jump. It plays the active state and blends to another state when a transition condition evaluates to true. Use a state machine to define which animations can follow each other without writing transition logic in Luau.

Each state connects to an input on the state machine. A state can be a clip, a blend node, or another state machine. The state machine outputs the active animation pose or a blend between two poses if transitioning, which you connect to the next node in the graph.

Prerequisites

Before you create a state machine, familiarize yourself with the Animation Graph Editor, including how to open it and create an animation graph.

Create a state machine

The following example uses three states from JumpFallLandRunExample: Locomotion, Fall, and LandIdle. The character moves normally, switches to a falling animation when airborne, and plays a landing animation before returning to locomotion. These steps focus on the state machine; start with animation nodes for locomotion, falling, and landing.

  1. In the Graph Editor, right-click and select Insert Node ⟩ State Machine.

  1. On the state machine node, click Open. In the State Machine view, use Create State to add three states named Locomotion, Fall, and LandIdle.

  1. Click Back to Graph and connect your animation nodes to the corresponding state machine inputs:
  2. Locomotion: Connect your locomotion animation. The reference graph uses an Blend1DNode named IdleRunBlend to blend idle and running animations based on Speed.
  3. Fall: Connect a falling ClipNode and set Play Mode to OnceAndHold, so it holds its final pose until the character lands.
  4. LandIdle: Connect a landing clip and set Play Mode to OnceAndHold, so it can finish and transition back to locomotion.

Connect the state machine output to the Pose input of Graph Output.

  1. Open the State Machine view again and drag a transition from (Entry) to Locomotion. The state machine starts in this state when the graph starts.

  1. Add a Boolean graph parameter named Grounded and set it to true. This parameter indicates whether the character is on the ground.

  2. Add the following transitions by dragging a connection from the source state to the destination state, then configure each transition:

  3. Locomotion to Fall: Set Wait For to Expression, Expression to not Grounded, and Length to 0.2 seconds. The falling animation begins when the character leaves the ground.
  4. Fall to LandIdle: Set Wait For to Expression, Expression to Grounded, and Length to 0.1 seconds. The landing animation begins when the character touches the ground.
  5. LandIdle to Locomotion: Set Wait For to Finished, When to BeforeFinished, and Length to 0.2 seconds. The state machine begins blending back to locomotion during the final 0.2 seconds of the landing animation.

  1. Leave Curve as the default (Linear) for all three transitions. Preview the graph and change Grounded to false to enter Fall, then back to true to play LandIdle and return to Locomotion.

  2. Update Grounded from your gameplay code as the character leaves and touches the ground. If your locomotion blend uses Speed, update that parameter as the character moves. For the parameter workflow, see API integration.

  3. Extend the state machine with jumping and additional landing states to create the full movement graph. JumpFallLandRunExample includes separate jumps for standing and running, plus different landings based on movement and fall speed.

For the full state machine, open JumpFallLandRunExample in the reference place.

State machine properties

State machine node properties

**Inputs**
- **State1...StateN**: The animation nodes that define each state. The name of the state must match the name of the input to the state machine node.
**Properties**
Property Type Description
**EntryState** ObjectValue An ObjectValue whose Value points to the AnimationNodeDefinition for the state that is active when the graph starts.
**Event data**
- **Event Handling:** Events from the active state pass through with their weight unchanged. - **Event Emission:** Passes through events from the active state only. During a transition, event emission follows the [global event rules](#/docs/animation/graph-editor).

Transition properties

A transition has one or more source states, a destination state, and a condition. When the active state matches a source state, the state machine checks the condition. It blends to the destination state when the condition evaluates to true.

Wait For determines the transition condition UI. Select Expression (Trigger) to display an Expression box. An Expression can reference a boolean graph parameter directly, such as ShouldJump, or evaluate a condition, such as Speed >= 12. Select Finished (Finished) to display the When dropdown.

If more than one transition has a true Expression, the state machine evaluates the transition with the highest Priority value first. When priorities are the same, it selects one transition at random. Assign different priorities to competing transitions to make the result predictable.

Property Type Description
**From** ObjectValue An ObjectValue whose Value points to the AnimationNodeDefinition for the state that can begin the transition. Leave this property unset for an **(Any)** transition.
**To** ObjectValue An ObjectValue whose Value points to the AnimationNodeDefinition for the destination state.
**WaitFor** AnimationNodeWaitFor Determines which transition condition UI appears. Trigger displays the **Expression** box. Finished displays the **When** dropdown.
**When** AnimationNodeTransitionWhen Available when **Wait For** is **Finished**. Select Finished to begin after the source state finishes, or BeforeFinished to begin blending one **Duration** before the source state finishes.
**Expression** String Available when **Wait For** is [**Expression**](#/docs/animation/expressions). A boolean graph parameter or expression that, when it evaluates to `true`, begins the transition. See [**Expression**](#/docs/animation/expressions) for what's supported.
**Priority** Number The order used when more than one **Expression** is true. Higher values take precedence. Valid values range from 0 to 65,535.
**Duration** Number The time, in seconds, to blend into the destination state. The default is 0.15 seconds.
**Curve** Enum.PoseEasingStyle The easing used during the blend. Only Linear and CubicV2 are supported. The default is Linear.

kid.simple: A state machine is a node in the Animation Graph Editor that holds named states, like Idle, Walk, Fall, and Land, and plays one at a time. You draw arrows (transitions) between states and give each arrow a rule, like "go to Fall when not Grounded". When the rule becomes true, it smoothly blends to the next state. This lets you build a full jump-fall-land system without writing the switching logic in code.
kid.analogy: It is like a board game path: you are always on one square, and arrows show which squares you can move to next and what you need (like rolling a 6) to move there.
keyPoints: Add one with right-click, Insert Node, State Machine, then click Open and use Create State to add states like `Locomotion`, `Fall`, and `LandIdle`.
Back in the graph, connect an animation node to each state's input, and connect the state machine output to Graph Output's Pose.
Drag from (Entry) to the state that should play first when the graph starts.
Transitions with Wait For set to Expression switch when a rule is true, like `not Grounded` or `Speed >= 12`.
Transitions with Wait For set to Finished switch when the current animation ends, or with When set to BeforeFinished, start blending a little before it ends.
Clips like falling and landing should use Play Mode OnceAndHold so they hold their last pose.
If several rules are true at once, the transition with the highest Priority (0 to 65,535) wins; ties are random.
Duration is the blend time in seconds (default 0.15), and Curve is Linear (default) or CubicV2. Update parameters like `Grounded` from your script.

terms.state machine: A system that is always in exactly one state and moves between states when rules are met.
terms.state: One named mode, like Idle or Fall, that plays a certain animation.
terms.transition: An arrow from one state to another, with a rule for when to switch.
terms.entry state: The state that starts playing when the graph begins.
terms.expression: A short formula that gives true or false, like `Speed >= 12`, used as a transition rule.
terms.Boolean: A value that is only `true` or `false`, like `Grounded`.
terms.OnceAndHold: Play the clip one time, then freeze on its last pose instead of looping.
terms.BeforeFinished: Start blending to the next state before the current one ends. With a 0.2-second length, the blend starts in the last 0.2 seconds.
terms.priority: A number that decides which transition wins if several are ready at once. Higher wins.
terms.Any transition: A transition with no From state set, so it can start from any state.
terms.locomotion: Normal moving around, like idle, walk, and run blended by speed.

example.title: Tell the graph if the character is on the ground
example.place: LocalScript in StarterCharacterScripts (graph loaded on this character, AuthorityMode Automatic)
example.code:
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local character = script.Parent
local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")
local animator = humanoid:WaitForChild("Animator")

-- Load your published graph (replace the ID)
local animation = Instance.new("Animation")
animation.AnimationId = "rbxassetid://123456789"
local graphTrack = animator:LoadAnimation(animation)
graphTrack:Play()

RunService.Stepped:Connect(function()
	-- FloorMaterial is Air when nothing is under the character
	local grounded = humanoid.FloorMaterial ~= Enum.Material.Air
	graphTrack:SetParameter("Grounded", grounded)
	-- Also feed speed for the idle/run blend
	graphTrack:SetParameter("Speed", humanoid.MoveDirection.Magnitude * humanoid.WalkSpeed)
end)
explain: We load and play the published graph on the character's `Animator`.
Every frame, we check `FloorMaterial`. If it is `Air`, the character is not standing on anything.
We send `Grounded` as true or false. When it turns false, the Locomotion to Fall rule `not Grounded` becomes true.
When the character lands, `Grounded` becomes true again, so Fall switches to LandIdle, which then blends back to Locomotion.
We also send `Speed` so the Locomotion state can blend idle and run.

watchOut: State names must match the input names on the state machine node exactly.
Forgetting the (Entry) arrow. The machine needs to know which state to start in.
Two transitions that can both be true with the same Priority. Give them different priorities so the result is not random.
Leaving falling or landing clips on a looping play mode. Use OnceAndHold so they hold the last pose.
Never updating `Grounded` from a script. The graph cannot know you jumped unless your code tells it.
